'''Martin Charles Golumbic''' (born 1948){{r|born}} is a [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]] known for his research on [[perfect graph]]s, [[graph sandwich problem]]s, [[tolerance graph]]s, [[compiler optimization]], and [[spatial-temporal reasoning]]. He is a [[professor emeritus]] of computer science at the [[University of Haifa]],{{r|haifabio}} and was the founder of the journal ''Annals of Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence''.

==Education and career==
Golumbic majored in mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]], graduating in 1970 with bachelor's and master's degrees.{{r|ae}} He completed his Ph.D. at [[Columbia University]] in 1975, with the dissertation ''Comparability Graphs and a New Matroid'' supervised by [[Samuel Eilenberg]].{{r|mg}}

He became an assistant professor in the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] of [[New York University]] from 1975 until 1980, when he moved to [[Bell Laboratories]]. From 1983 to 1992 he worked for [[IBM Research]] in Israel, and from 1992 to 2000 he was a professor of mathematics and computer science at [[Bar-Ilan University]]. He moved to the [[University of Haifa]] in 2000, where he founded the Caesarea Edmond Benjamin de Rothschild Institute for Interdisciplinary Applications of Computer Science.{{r|ae|haifabio}}

In 1989, Golumbic founded the Bar-Ilan Symposium in Foundations of Artificial Intelligence, a leading artificial intelligence conference in Israel.{{r|bisfai}} In 1990 Golumbic became the founding editor-in-chief of the journal ''Annals of Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence'', published by [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]].{{r|amai}}

==Recognition==
Golumbic is a fellow of the [[European Association for Artificial Intelligence]] (2005).{{r|eurai}} He was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2013.

At the 2019 Bar-Ilan Symposium in Foundations of Artificial Intelligence, Golumbic was given the Lifetime Achievement and Service Award of the Israeli Association for Artificial Intelligence.{{r|bisfai}}

==Selected publications==

=== Books ===
*''Algorithmic Graph Theory and Perfect Graphs'' (Academic Press, 1980; 2nd ed., Elsevier, 2004){{r|agt}}
*''Tolerance Graphs'' (with [[Ann Trenk]], Cambridge University Press, 2004){{r|tg}}
*''Fighting Terror Online: The Convergence of Security, Technology, and the Law'' (Springer, 2008){{r|fto}}
*''The Zeroth Book of Graph Theory: An Annotated Translation of Les Réseaux (ou Graphes)-[[André Sainte-Laguë]] (1926)'' (Springer, 2021){{r|zbgt}}
